p:cNvPr.descr: An image depicting the glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate dehydrogenase reaction. At the top left is NAD+. To the right is an arrow pointing to the right. Glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate merges into this arrow. This is step 1: Formation of enzyme-substrate complex. The active-site Cys has a reduced pKa (5.5 instead of 8) when NAD+ is bound, and is in the more reactive, thiolate form. This points to CH2OPO3 with a minus 2 cahrge, bonding down to HCOH, which bonds down to C, which double bonds down and right to L and bonds down and left to H. A red arrow points from the double bond down to O. Below this is S- bonding down to Cys. To the top left of all this is NAD+. The negative sign has a red arrow pointing from it to up to C. Below this is an arrow pointing down. This is step 2: A covalent thiohemiacetal linkage forms between the substrate and the –S- group of the Cys residue. CH2OPO3 with a minus 2 charge bonds down to HCOH, which bonds down to C, which bonds right to O-, left to H, and down to S, which bonds down to Cys. A red arrow points from the negative sign on O, which points to the bond between C and O-. Another red arrow points from the C to H bond line that points up to NAD+. Below this is an arrow pointing down. This is step 3: The enzyme-substrate intermediate is oxidized by the NAD+ bound to the active site. Below this is CH2OPO3 with a minus 2 charge bonding down to HCOH, which bonds down to C, which double bonds right to O and bonds down to S, which bonds down to Cys. To the left of this is an arrow pointing left. Above this, NAD+ merges with this arrow, as does Pi (in pink). Below the arrow is another arrow pointing to NADH. This is step 4: The NADH product leaves the active site and is replaced by another molecule of NAD+. This points to CH2OPO3 with a minus 2 charge bonds down to HCOH, which bonds down to C, which double bonds right to O and bonds down to S, which bonds down to Cys. To the right is P which double bonds up to O, bonds right to OH, down to O-, and left to O- (all in pink). A red arrow points from the O- to C. Another red arrow points from the bond line between C and S to S. Above this is an arrow pointing up, which also has an arrow pointing left to 1.3-bisphosphoglycerate, where CH2OPO3 with am inus 2 charge bonds down to HCOH, which bonds down to C, which double bonds right to O and bonds down to OPO3 with a minus 2 charge (in pink). This is step 5: The covalent thioester linkage between the substrate and enzyme undergoes phosphorolysis (attack by Pi), releasing the second product, 1,3-bisphophoglycerate. Above and to the left of the arrow is S- bonding down to Cys.
